extracted.intended_audience: Department of Defense policymakers, military medical services managers, productivity analysts, and academic researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for designing, reporting, and interpreting productivity measures for the military health care delivery system (Composite Work Unit, Adjusted Admission Equivalent, indices, and policy/reporting requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD Productivity Program policy statements (Directive 5010.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: Directive set forth important long-range Productivity Program policy statements for the Department of Defense including: (1) The program will direct '...management attention on achieving maximum Defense outputs within available resources levels by seeking out and exploiting opportunities for improved methods of operation.' (2) 'Productivity measurement, enhancement, and evaluation will be an integral element of resource management.' (3) The benefits of productivity enhancement '...should be re-utilized at the lowest level practical to provide an incentive for management...' and to accent focus on labor cost savings efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are policy-level evaluative goals: measures should be oriented to maximizing outputs given resources; measurement/enhancement must be integrated with resource management and budgeting; and realized gains should be returned at low organizational levels as incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirements of DoD Instruction 5010.34
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction provided for: establishment of a requirement for productivity goals at all levels; requirements of productivity measurement reporting and evaluation; and guidance on work methods, workload measurement, and productivity enhancing capital investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement systems and local management must set annual productivity goals, report measurement data, evaluate results, and consider capital investment that enhances productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enclosure mandate for permanent productivity measurement system (Enclosure 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enclosure mandates the establishment of a permanent system for measuring and evaluating productivity for the Department of Defense under the Federal productivity reporting system for input to the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). The measure value submitted was to be 'in the form of a productivity index: "The relationship between the volume of goods produced or services rendered and the quantity of resources consumed..."' Responsibility assigned to the Assistant Secretary of Defense (Manpower, Reserve Affairs and Logistics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD measurements must be compatible with Federal reporting (BLS) and be deliverable as productivity indices (outputs relative to inputs). Assign responsibility and reporting channels accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of major function indices and labor-produced index preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Today, major function indices are used within DoD 'to determine the extent of productivity coverage in the major commands and operating agencies of DOD Components.' The enclosure noted that 'A labor-produced index is the type of productivity index most frequently developed, partly because labor is universally required in accomplishing all types of work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize labor-based indices where appropriate because labor is central and commonly measurable; but ensure indices cover relevant functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and functional classification for medical measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section defined scope: 'Medical-Hospitals. This area covers personnel performing all types of medical and dental procedures and services in hospitals and medical centers.' 'Medical-Clinics. This area covers personnel performing all types of medical and dental procedures and services in clinics.' Suggested indicators included the 'Health Care Composite Unit' and the similar 'Adjusted Admission Equivalent (USAF)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define measurement scope explicitly (hospital vs clinic, dental vs non-dental) and select appropriate indicator (Composite Work Unit, AAE) for that scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectiveness Measures—'Comparison of current performance against pre-established mission objectives (goals).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measures that show attainment of mission objectives (outcomes, goal achievement), not just activity counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency Measures—'Comparison of current performance against either a pre-established standard or actual performance of a prior period.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standards or historical baselines to assess whether the same outputs are being produced with fewer or similar inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor Productivity Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Labor Productivity Measures—'Comparison of same performance during two periods of time, usually a current period and a previous period, known as a base period. It compares actual manpower expended and the resulting products produced, or services rendered during the two periods of time and discloses the labor performance of an activity or group of individuals during the current period in relation to their performance during a previous period of time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trend labor inputs versus outputs over time; use base periods for comparison and ensure consistency of definitions across periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative (Standard-based) Productivity Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative Productivity Measures—'Comparison of labor performance against pre-established standards. It compares actual manpower expenses on a job or task during a given period of time with the standard established for the job or task for that period of time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop defensible standards (time/effort per task) and compare actuals to standards to identify deviations and improvement opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity index formula and design considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplistic equation generally used: Productivity Index = Outputs / Inputs. The most critical task in designing a productivity ratio is deciding what factors the output and input elements should contain, realizing that there may not be only one 'useful' answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly define and document what is counted as outputs and inputs; choose elements suited to the application and be transparent about tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for comparability and evaluation relative to input changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Productivity measurements in and of themselves do not generally provide any useful information concerning efficiency. Rather, to provide useful information, the measures must be capable of being compared to note the differences in production over specific time periods and to be evaluated in relationship to the changes in inputs required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design measures to support comparative analysis (over time or across units) and always interpret output changes in the context of input changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive patterns for changes in computed productivity ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Productivity 'improvements,' as measured by changes in the computed ratios, can occur in any of the following combinations: 1) Increase output/input remains stable or constant; 2) Increase output/decrease input; 3) Increase output at a rate greater than the corresponding input element; 4) Stable or constant output/input decreases; 5) Decrease output at a lesser rate than the corresponding decreasing input element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When observing index changes, analyze whether changes arose from outputs rising, inputs falling, or differing rates — and beware of misinterpreting declines or increases without decomposing components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output conceptualizations: process (activity) vs outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Output of the health care system can generally be viewed as either a process or an outcome. Process view treats outputs as medical care itself, using surrogate/proxy elements (physician visits, admissions, bed days, studies, births, therapies). Outcome view treats output as patient health after care (improved health), which raises measurement challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit which conception is used. Process measures are more common and easier to collect; outcome measures may be more meaningful but have attribution, measurement, and comparability challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of surrogate/proxy elements for health care outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Common surrogates include number of physician visits, admissions, occupied bed days, studies performed, births, and therapies provided. These are used to define hospital 'products' (activities required for provision of health services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize each proxy's limitations (heterogeneity of services, intensity, case-mix) and document weights/assumptions when aggregating heterogeneous activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-based output approach and case-mix concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to use the hospital 'case' as an output (number of discharges). Raises questions: what is appropriate care or input into a case? What of case-mix variations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using cases/discharges as outputs, adjust or stratify for case-mix/severity to avoid misleading comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for excess or standby capacity and readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Donabedian noted that investment in hospital and personnel must include some excess (standby) capacity to be utilized when need occurs; physicians and nurses have standby time. Example: in a group practice each physician worked 42 hours and stood an additional 28 hours standby (40% standby).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and explicitly account for standby/ready capacity when allocating inputs or interpreting productivity (distinguish required standby for readiness from idle excess).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Work Unit (CWU) definition and component definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Composite Work Unit (Medical Care Composite Unit) defined (components): OBD = Occupied Bed Days; AD = Admissions; LB = Live Births; OPV = Outpatient Visits. The CWU weights reflected: one admission ≈ 10 occupied bed days; one live birth ≈ 10 patient days; three outpatient visits ≈ one occupied bed day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using CWU, apply the specified component definitions and weights consistently; be aware that services like telephone consultations count if entered in chart and classification is by medical care provided rather than professional level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusted Admission Equivalent (AAE) formula and hospital/clinic variants
rubrics_metrics.description: AAE (Air Force) formula example: Number of AAEs = ADM + .0150 PV + .016 DP + .003 LP ... where ADM = admissions, OPV/PV = outpatient visits, DP = dental visits, LP = laboratory procedures, PR = pharmaceutical prescriptions, XR = x-rays processed. Hospitals without dental services exclude dental component. AAE does not use occupied bed days but relies on admissions to account for inpatient workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAE provides a different weighted aggregation of activities; ensure facility type (with/without dental) is handled correctly and transparently report included components and weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-year weighting, conversion to weighted output, and index computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs are converted into a weighted output using base year weights (1977 used as base). Weights are established by equalizing output to employee-years in base year so that weighted output and employee-years equal numerically in base year. Each succeeding year’s input elements are converted to percentages based on base-year gross numbers (base year set at 100.000). Productivity per employee is computed by dividing weighted output (A) by employee-years (B), both based on their respective percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and document base year and weights; convert inputs/outputs to indices/percentages consistently; compute indices by dividing weighted outputs by employee-years or other input base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data submission and DPPO/BLS processing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Military services submit statistical data for workload measurement to the Department of Defense Productivity Program Office (DPPO). Composite Work Unit calculations, total manhours, and employee compensation are also submitted. DPPO and Bureau of Labor Statistics compute productivity indices (measured activities and total activities sections include measured, non-measured, and support activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish data collection processes to provide accurate CWU/AAE, employee-years, compensation, and other needed inputs to DPPO/BLS; follow accepted formats to ensure BLS-acceptable indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended uses of productivity measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Productivity measurement efforts emphasize importance for resource allocation, budgeting, manpower allocations, and capital expenditures, both on the local level and at higher organizational levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design measures with intended policy/management uses in mind (budgeting, staffing, capital planning) and ensure measures are actionable for those uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation principle: fit-for-purpose measurement system
rubrics_metrics.description: It may require that there be different systems for different applications. Therefore, each system considered for implementation should be evaluated on its merits in fulfilling its specific function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume a single 'best' measure; evaluate candidate systems against the specific decision-making needs, e.g., staffing allocation vs trend analysis vs external reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of measured vs total activities in indices (measured, non-measured, support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits are divided into two sections: measured activities and total activities. The total activities section contains the measured, non-measured, and support activities required to produce the indicated output quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting indices, provide both measured-activities-only and total-activities computations to illustrate completeness and the effect of non-measured/support activities on productivity.
